meta.description: Authored 1900 world for M11/M11b country selection: 67 polities (66 selectable), 66 dependent territories, and 20 documented markets. Population totals are rounded historical estimates; occupation composition, market grouping, building levels, fiscal and technology starts are provisional authored inputs; map geometry is Natural Earth 1:50m aggregated with an explicit 1900 crosswalk. Polities without reliable 1900 polygon data use marker-only map approximations. Not a full historical reconstruction.

Cisleithania (the Austrian half) and Transleithania (the Hungarian half, including Croatia-Slavonia) each had their own government; Bosnia and Herzegovina was jointly administered. There was no single unified national flag: the common civil ensign combines the Austrian red-white-red and Hungarian red-white-green with both coats of arms. Co-capital: Budapest. The map geometry covers the core modern units (Austria, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina); Galicia, Transylvania, Vojvodina and South Tyrol are not separable at the Natural Earth 1:50m admin-0 resolution.

Tonga was an independent kingdom on 1 January 1900 and became a British protectorate later in 1900 (Treaty of Friendship, 18 May 1900). M11c reconstructs its territory from the modern Tongan archipelago; the archipelago's extent is not disputed.

De facto independent with limited international recognition; conquered by British forces in 1903. M11c reconstructs the caliphate's core from ten modern northern Nigerian states. Population is a rounded order-of-magnitude estimate.

De facto independent with limited international recognition. M11c reconstructs the sultanate's core from modern Chadian regions; the northern Tibesti and southern tributary zones are excluded. M11c.1 uses the user-selected representative flag (white field with black border), classified as representative rather than an exact attested historical national flag. Population is a rounded estimate.

De facto independent with limited international recognition; the Anglo-Egyptian condominium did not control Darfur in 1900. M11c reconstructs the sultanate from the modern Darfur states as a conservative core. M11c.1 uses the user-selected representative flag (green-red-black triband with white crescent), classified as representative rather than an exact attested historical national flag. Population is a rounded estimate.

De facto independent and nominally Ottoman; conquered by Ibn Saud in 1921. M11c reconstructs the emirate from Ha'il, Qassim, Riyadh, the Northern Borders and al-Jowf; Ottoman sovereignty over Najd was nominal. Population is a rounded estimate.

Internationally recognised autonomous state, not a fully independent sovereign country (the 1913 union with Greece is after the reference date). M11c separates Crete from modern Greece using the modern Crete region. The flag combines the Greek cross with a red canton and white star.
